body:
Not sure if this can be classified as a bug but I thought I would post this just incase it isn't known about. Values known at compile time, and are thus computed in Python, use Python's long int and can represent values outside the range of a normal integer so you can get results that don't quite match.

```
from numba import cuda
import numpy as np

@cuda.jit
def test_kernel(a,b,c,test):
	i = cuda.grid(1)

	test[0] = a**b%c
	test[1] = 11**19%1009

a, b, c = 11, 19, 1009
test = cuda.device_array(2, dtype = np.uint32)

test_kernel[1, 1](a,b,c,test)

print(a**b%c,test.copy_to_host())
>>> 902 [759 902]
```
title: Runtime integer calculation overflow
